column3: A music box: a brass cylinder studded with pins turns and plucks a steel comb. The pins on the drum are the time, and you see them come round and pluck. On the minute the drum is re-pinned.
An Etch A Sketch: two knobs drive a stylus that draws the time as one continuous line. On the minute the toy is shaken, the line crumbles away as aluminium powder, and the knobs redraw.

A crew of tiny hand-drawn workers (Lemmings-style builders, diggers, blockers) who build the time out of bricks and tear it down again, each with a job and a personality. Playful and character-driven.
Cat's cradle: two pairs of hands hold a loop of string, and the string figure between them is the time. On the minute the fingers pass the loops across and the figure transforms.
A digital water curtain: valves along a bar release drops in patterns, so the time appears in falling water and splashes into a pool below.
Tangram: seven flat pieces per digit slide, spin and flip to rebuild the numerals. Make the motion choreographed and physical, with weight and shadow.
A marionette theatre: the digits are puppets hanging on strings from a wooden control bar worked by an unseen hand. They dance, slump and are re-strung into the next number.

A fogged window at night: someone breathes on the glass and a fingertip writes the time in the condensation. Drops run down from the strokes, and the fog creeps back. On the minute a new breath fogs the glass and the finger writes again.
A bonsai tree: branches grow, are wired and bend into the shape of the time, with leaves on them. On the minute leaves fall and new growth forms the new digit. The hour is a season.
Light painting: a small character waves a sparkler in a long exposure, and the glowing trail writes the time. Sparks fly off, and the trail fades as the next stroke is drawn.
Soap bubbles: a wand blows bubbles whose films (swirling dithered interference bands) take the shape of the digits. They wobble and drift, and on the minute they pop and are re-blown.

A sushi conveyor belt (kaiten-zushi) running along the strip: cute plates and sushi characters ride by carrying the time, and a chef's hands swap the plates out on the minute. (128x32 strip: design for the panorama shape; the 0.91" board is I2C-only, so use bus i2c400 at 50 fps; you may draw into hidden RAM with ramPages: 8 and use hardware scroll.)
